chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from al-Ahwal, from Humran who said:

I heard Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, the disbelievers and polytheists will taunt the monotheists in the Fire, saying: We do not see how your monotheism benefited you in any way; you and we are equal.'

So the Lord, Exalted and Majestic, will feel disdain for them and will say to the angels: 'Intercede,' so they will intercede for whom Allah wills. And He will say to the believers: 'Do likewise,' until no one remains but that the intercession reaches him.
He, the Blessed and Exalted, will say: 'I am the Most Merciful of the merciful. Come out by My mercy,' so they will come out like moths.
He said: Then Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Then the columns will be extended and fixed over them, and it will be, by Allah, eternity.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to monotheists who enter Hellfire according to the hadith of intercession?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* elucidates the Shia doctrine of *Khuruj min al-Nar* (exit from Hell), emphasizing that intercession (*shafa'ah*) is a divine mercy extending to monotheists who committed sins but retained faith. The narrative highlights the psychological torment of disbelievers witnessing the salvation of the faithful, culminating in God’s declaration of being 'the most merciful of the merciful' to extract them, after which the structural pillars of Hell are fixed over the remaining inhabitants for eternity.
